evidence_quotes.agenda: No formal their-agenda question asked, but customer spontaneously raised three real concerns (hidden fees, TV handling, and insurance for a valuable ceramic grill).
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Genuine two-layer follow-up on the grill/insurance concern specifically: rep reassured on mover training, then fully explained the $2,000 no-worry damage coverage and confirmed it's included in the quoted rate until customer said 'awesome, okay' — scored on the merits, not the no-concern exception.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Explained the estimate is a window due to the extra grill-handling time; no commit-to-rate/100k line, no pay-less-if-faster, no self-prep tip, no fair-check (call ended before booking — customer needed to confirm the house purchase first).

top_strength: Validated the customer's concern directly ('that's a very valid concern') and delivered the damage-coverage differentiator in direct, specific response to his real worry — textbook Stage 1 answer-a-raised-concern execution.
coaching_note: Make the explicit close ask before the call drifts into an open-ended 'I'll call you back' — the customer was clearly engaged and this was a good opportunity to at least offer to hold the date.
